clue.text: The French gentleman is excused

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
a toff is British slang for an upper-class gent

explanation.surface: A French nobleman is let off some duty or other.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh, well-to-do man.
explanation.definitionFit: To be let off is to be pardoned or spared a penalty, the phrasal-verb synonym of excused.

clue.text: Call to observe employment for bloodsucker

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold
use, as in putting something to use, means employment

explanation.surface: Someone shouts to watch a worker, but the worker turns out to be a parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: The louse is a small parasitic insect that feeds on the blood of its host.

clue.text: Intoxicate a giant, by report

indicators.note: by report signals that the word for a giant is heard rather than written

parts.note: a Titan is one of the giant deities of Greek myth

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to get a giant drunk, or so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: TIGHT is British slang for drunk, so to make someone tight is to intoxicate them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal for drunk, so making someone tighter is getting them inebriated.

clue.text: Alien rule held by enemy to the monarch

indicators.note: held by means the word for rule sits inside the word for enemy

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
a reign is a period of rule
R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: An outsider's rule is endured by those hostile to the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a person from another country, an outsider by nationality.

clue.text: Ancient city, almost No.1

indicators.note: almost means the phrase for number one loses its final letter

parts.note: number one, the top, is the best

explanation.surface: A classical city is described as very nearly the finest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter from THE BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great city of both ancient Egypt and ancient Greece.

clue.text: A lot of colour in the centre of damp

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word for colour is used

parts.note: a hue is a colour or shade
mid means middle or centre

explanation.surface: A painter notes a patch of strong colour in the middle of a damp area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' drops the last letter of HUE, leaving HU.
explanation.definitionFit: Humid air is moist, heavy with water vapour.

clue.text: Englishwoman not allowed to be a wailer?

parts.note: something not allowed is under a ban
she is the pronoun for a woman
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman is barred, and perhaps howls about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'Englishwoman' gives both E and SHE, set down as SHE then E.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore the banshee is a spirit whose keening cry foretells a death.

clue.text: Noisy rite used to establish precedence

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are used to build something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loud ceremony is held to settle who ranks above whom.
explanation.definitionFit: Seniority is priority by rank or length of service, which is precedence.

clue.text: First of all in poor country

indicators.note: in means the opening letter is placed inside the word for poor

parts.note: the poor go hungry, lacking food

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Above all, the people of a poor nation are struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of all' looks like 'primarily', but it gives the A of 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungary is a central European nation.

clue.text: Distinguished artist Tracey's turned 10

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist, so her surname is given

indicators.note: turned means the letters of the number word that follows are rearranged

parts.note: ten written as a word

explanation.surface: A celebrated artist has just turned ten years old.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a famous British artist; 'turned' rearranges TEN to ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent people are notable and respected, standing out in their field.

clue.text: Spooner's "Reject the play area" when bad light stopped the 23?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: to ditch is to throw away or reject
a park is an area for recreation and play

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism about rejecting a playground, tied to a sports match halted by poor light.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of DITCH PARK gives PITCH DARK. The 23 is CRICKET, where play stops for bad light.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch-dark means utterly black, the kind of gloom that makes umpires halt a game.

clue.text: Fringe diet unexpectedly adopted by the middle classes

indicators.note: unexpectedly means the letters of the two words end up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: An alternative eating plan has suddenly caught on with the bourgeoisie.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentrified area has been taken over and remade by affluent newcomers.

clue.text: The pirate of Holland?

parts.note: joins the villainous captain of Peter Pan and the Dutch port called the same, as if one were from the other

explanation.surface: A question about a Dutch buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan; the Hook of Holland is a Dutch ferry port.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to J M Barrie's one-handed captain and to a headland and port on the Dutch coast.

clue.text: Cloth made from wool in England

indicators.note: made from means the answer is built from a run of letters inside the next words

explanation.surface: A fabric woven from English wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is fabric woven from flax.

clue.text: They have locals left with

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'They have locals left with (9)', gives L + AND for 'left with' but no word for LORDS; the clue appears cut short (probably a cross-reference to the cricket ground) and no source restores it.

clue.text: Space traveller in universal setting purely for show

indicators.note: in means the space traveller is put inside the word for universal

parts.note: cosmic means relating to the whole universe
ET is the alien of Spielberg's film, a traveller from space

explanation.surface: An alien in a cosmic scene is just there for appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' is the surrounding word, COSMIC, into which ET goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic changes are superficial, affecting looks rather than substance.

clue.text: Just weight for fool

parts.note: just, as in merely, can mean simple
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Weight alone is used to describe a dunce.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, gullible person.

clue.text: Find out about the unusual and invisible

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the word for unusual
out means the letters of find are rearranged

parts.note: something unusual is rare

explanation.surface: Someone discovers something odd that cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find out' reads as discover, but 'out' is the anagram signal on Find alone, and 'about' says that shuffled word wraps round the word for unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared radiation lies beyond red in the spectrum, outside the range of human sight.

clue.text: Polish picture crucially crossed

parts.note: to rub something is to polish it
an icon is a picture, especially a holy image

explanation.surface: A Polish painting was decisively traversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the nationality, but it is the verb. Caesar crossing the Rubicon river committed him to civil war.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the Rubicon means taking a decisive, irreversible step, as Caesar did with that river.

clue.text: Greek character, reserved and sentimental

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
shy means reserved or timid

explanation.surface: A Greek man is described as quiet and soppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushy means overly soft-hearted or sloppy in feeling.

clue.text: Southern peninsula between continents

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A southern peninsula is said to lie on the border of two landmasses.
explanation.definitionFit: This vast Russian region spans northern Asia, lying between Europe and North America across the Bering Strait.

clue.text: See 21
Care centre, luckily bomb damaged, initially makes I cubic metre

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the four words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A care centre is fortunately only damaged by a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: The club's initials MCC can be read as M (a million) cc, cubic centimetres, which is one cubic metre.
explanation.definitionFit: The club is the historic owner of Lord's and guardian of the laws of the sport; its initials are MCC.

clue.text: I don't believe what tells me what I see

definitions.text: what tells me what I see

explanation.surface: Someone doubts what their own senses report.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My eye!' is an old exclamation of disbelief, and literally the organ of sight reports what one sees.

clue.text: A funny thing happened after sunset

definitions.text: A funny thing happened after sunset

parts.words: A funny thing happened after sunset
parts.note: echoes the stand-up opener about a funny thing happening, but really just names the dark period that follows sundown

explanation.surface: A comedian starts a story about the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours that follow the sun going down.

clue.text: See 21
Preservation of gold in the theatre

indicators.note: in means the word for gold goes inside the word for the theatre

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold is kept somewhere in the playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is keeping things for future use, a way of preserving them.

clue.text: It goes down in connection with 12 and most of 13 across

definitions.text: in connection with 12 and most of 13 across

explanation.surface: Something sinks in connection with two other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is HOOK and most of 13 is LINE(N), giving the phrase hook, line and ___, meaning completely.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight that drags a fishing line under the water, and the last item in the idiom hook, line and its partner.

clue.text: Home enthusiast has time for baby

parts.note: in means at home
a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A keen supporter stays in, minding the baby.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child.
